picks.name: The Gifter
picks.why_plausible: The brief says candles are 'mostly bought as gifts' and this persona is any shopper in gifting mode with low price sensitivity and high AOV. Hand-poured Vermont candles are exactly the 'impressive-looking' giftable object they seek.
picks.ad_angle: The gift that always lands: a hand-poured Vermont candle that looks more expensive than it is.

picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: Affinities include home_goods and she responds to craftsmanship, heritage and quality over trends — a match for small-batch, hand-poured, Made in Vermont. Low price sensitivity fits a premium $40 candle.
picks.ad_angle: Old-fashioned craft: poured by hand in small batches in Vermont, the way candles used to be made.

picks.name: The Sustainability Buyer
picks.why_plausible: Home_goods affinity plus values overlap on clean_ingredients and heritage; natural soy wax and no synthetic fragrances are the specific, non-vague claims they want. Medium price sensitivity is fine at $40.
lean_into: specific claims: soy wax, no synthetic fragrance
picks.ad_angle: Specific, not vague: soy wax, no synthetic fragrance, poured in small batches in one Vermont workshop.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: Wellness affinity and clean-ingredient values line up with 'no synthetic fragrances' in a product she burns in her home nightly. Low price sensitivity supports a premium candle as a self-treat.
picks.ad_angle: What you breathe at home matters: a clean-burning soy candle with nothing synthetic in the scent.

plan.summary: No candle competitors in the catalog, so the plan rests on two home and self-care tests — Northbed and Studiogrid — plus a promoted look at Hearthstone Goods, whose gifting and non-toxic notes the category tags undercounted.

test.name: Northbed
test.adjustment_reason: Notes cite 'High cross-sell with home and wellness', a direct adjacency the category tag only partially credited for a home-fragrance product.
test.rationale: Bedding and bath buyers are the closest thing in the catalog to a home-fragrance audience, and the notes' 'Design-conscious urban/suburban buyers' match the brand's handmade, aesthetic positioning.

evidence.quote: High cross-sell with home and wellness

test.risk: At $164 typical orders a $40 candle is a small add-on, and 3.6M impressions cap the volume of any test.

test.name: Hearthstone Goods
test.adjustment_reason: Notes say 'Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase' and the non_toxic subcategory matches the brand's no-synthetic-fragrance claim — both under-credited by a fuzzy kitchen category match.
test.rationale: Sustainability-motivated home buyers shopping for gifts and new homes are a natural audience for a $40 hand-poured Vermont candle, even though the kitchen subcategory scores as only a loose match.

evidence.quote: Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase

test.risk: Only 2.8M impressions and a $198 typical order mean low volume and a big price gap.

test.name: Studiogrid
test.rationale: Spa and yoga bookers are 'actively spending on self-care', which is exactly the self-treat candle purchase, and the $42 average order sits right on the $40 price point.

evidence.quote: Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness

test.risk: Appointment-booking confirmations are a service context, not a shopping one, so gift intent may be weaker than on product checkouts.

bid_strategy.rationale: $40 first order (assumed) × 0.30 = $12.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: Assumed a first order around $40 since no pricing was given.
Assumed one-time purchases rather than a subscription.
Assumed a broad adult audience of home and gift shoppers.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
